sam: Quick bring-up for Verdigris-9B quant experiments. Ran fp16 / int8 / int6 / int4 across a mixed slice (N=240: long-form summarization, multi-turn QA, short chat). TL;DR: int6 yields strong unit-econ wins with minimal short-chat impact; int4 shows consistent compression on stepwise instructions.

ivy: please drop the mini-scorecard + deltas (metrics: ROUGE-L / median latency @1024 / est $/1k).

sam: short table below (aggregate):
```
variant | ROUGE-L | p50 ms | cost($/1k)
fp16    | 0.739   | 155    | 1.00
int8    | 0.733   | 125    | 0.68
int6    | 0.728   | 105    | 0.56
int4    | 0.705   | 85     | 0.38

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.5% ROUGE-L, -32% p50, -44% cost
delta int4 vs fp16: -4.5% ROUGE-L, -45% p50, -62% cost
```

noah: what failure modes did you see at int6 vs int4?

sam: quick triage: int6 regressions (long-doc QA) -> 58% loss of intermediate steps (abstractive compression), 30% small factual drift on numerics, 12% tone concision. int4 adds more severe omissions and occasional hallucinated entities. Short chat (<64 tokens) is basically indistinguishable across int8/int6.

immediately: latency tails? 95/99p?

sam: 95p: fp16 420ms, int8 330ms, int6 290ms, int4 250ms. 99p: fp16 780ms, int6 540ms, int4 480ms. Lower precision tightens tails (packing + fewer evictions).

maria: product wants a routing recommendation for GTN and rollout gates.

sam: proposed routing: default verdigris-9b-int6; route to fp16 when input_tokens > 400 OR request_tag == "high_recall" OR route == "legal/financial". Keep int4 for internal batch summarization only (manual audit required).

sam: sample rule: {"routing": {"default_model": "verdigris-9b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 400}, "model": "verdigris-9b-fp16"}, {"match": {"request_tag": "high_recall"}, "model": "verdigris-9b-fp16"}]}}

ivy: rollout gates: accept int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute on long-doc holdout AND hallucination increase <= 3 percentage points AND manual spot-check shows no end-to-end correctness regressions on 50 sampled tasks. Block int4 for high-recall.

noah: ops notes: int6 kernels available on standard fleets but we should validate scheduling impact for packed batches. Recommend canary 5% + 24h shadowing + auto-eval hook for ROUGE/hallucination that fails rollout. int4 needs vendor runtime validation on dedicated pool before any wider use.

sam: econ sketch (toy): baseline all fp16 $75k/mo. With 80% int6, 15% int8, 5% fp16 => ~$52k/mo (~31% savings). With a 10% quality buffer -> plan $57k/mo. Slide will be prepared for GTN.

ci-bot: Canary created: canary/verdigris-int6-2024-11-20 (traffic 5%). See /deploys/20442

maria: great. please attach holdout queries and a few annotated failure examples in the canary ticket; GTN will want to review before wider rollout. We'll reconvene after 24h metrics.
